summary: Session-affinity refresh vs GPU-pool rebalance causing intermittent region egress and cost bump
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports sudden increase in egress to ap-south-1 for a tenant pinned to eu-west-1 following routine GPU pool rebalancing. Behavior began intermittently on 2026-03-12 after an autoscaler rebalance window.

Impact:
- Observed 2x token cost bump for a subset (~12%) of requests over 24h for FableAI's dedicated pool.
- P95 latency increased from ~110ms to ~270ms on affected requests.
- No explicit configuration changes from customer side.

Environment:
- Customer: FableAI (dedicated capacity)
- Region: primary eu-west-1 serving; anomalous egress seen to ap-south-1
- Models: rw-inference-v1 for most traffic; llm-opt-13b for heavy queries

Steps to reproduce (customer observed):
1) Send steady traffic (~200 rps) pinned to tenant pool in eu-west-1.
2) During autoscaler scheduled rebalance window (03:00–04:00 UTC), intermittent requests route out-of-region.
3) Cost and latency for those requests spike.

Observed behavior:
- Affected requests show two-phase path: edge -> eu-west control plane -> ap-south serving node (multi-hop).
- Logs contain session-affinity refresh events immediately prior to hop.

Expected behavior:
- Sticky session affinity to tenant's eu-west pool should keep egress in-region unless a hard failover/fallback triggers.

Relevant logs/links:
- Customer-provided traces: https://s3.redwood.ai/fableai/traces/2026-03-12-eh2q.zip
- Kibana dashboard: https://kibana.redwood.ai/d/fableai/egress-hop-analysis
- Billing spike window: invoice line items 2026-03-12 to 2026-03-13

Notes: customer is concerned both about data residency (they must keep egress in EU) and the unexpected billing delta.

investigation_notes: Control-plane correlates: during pool rebalances the scheduler moves fraction of GPU-allocated containers to new hosts; ephemeral token used by routing to refresh session-affinity may be issued on a control-plane instance in a different region causing path flip.
We observed affinity refresh requests hitting a metadata endpoint that resolved to a global control-plane VIP which returned a region-ambiguous stamp when the local scheduler was in state TRANSITION.

Heap of affected requests share same short-lived client hint header (X-Req-Sticky=short). Hypothesis: short TTL + scheduler movement => affinity refresh races with host eviction and control-plane instance selection, producing stale residency stamp.
Billing analysis: average egress cost per affected request increased by 0.004 USD; multiplied by traffic proportion explains reported invoice delta.
Related internal ticket INT-1402 tracks a recent scheduler change to host drain semantics during rebalance (PR #2184 referenced).
resolution: Mitigation applied: increased session-affinity TTL for tenant 'fableai-tenant-42' from 30s to 5m to reduce race window during rebalances. Customer notified. Next steps: engineering to land a control-plane fix to ensure affinity refreshes inherit explicit region stamp (work tracked in INT-1402 / PR #2184). Post-mortem and a billing credit proposal pending after verification.
